story_type: astronauts practice Moon landings by flying helicopters onto mountain ridges
hook: Astronauts land helicopters on peaks to practice for the Moon.
narration: To practice Moon landings, NASA astronauts fly helicopters onto Colorado mountaintops.
In August 2025, astronauts Matthew Dominick and Mark Vande Hei trained with the Army National Guard near Gypsum, Colorado.
Up here the air is thin, the terrain is jagged, and the wind keeps shifting.
Like a Moon lander, this helicopter flies on thin power margins, with controls that react almost like thruster firings.
Guard instructors and the astronauts took turns flying, while NASA lander experts rode along.
On the radio, the call-outs count down the last few feet. Twelve, ten, nine, eight, seven.
outcome: After two weeks, NASA certified the course to train astronauts for Artemis Moon landings.
title: Astronauts land helicopters on peaks
description:
In late August 2025, NASA astronauts Matthew Dominick and Mark Vande Hei flew helicopters with Colorado Army National Guard instructor pilots at the High-Altitude Army National Guard Aviation Training Site near Gypsum, Colorado, as NASA certified a lander flight training course for Artemis Moon missions.
